clue.text: Attack viciously? Proceed towards jail, having broken a rule wrongly

parts.note: to proceed is to go forth, to set out

indicators.note: the jail word breaks into the other letters, splitting them open
the letters of 'a rule' set down wrongly, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: jug is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Someone heading off to prison after misapplying a rule, as if pondering a ferocious assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' turns A RULE into EULAR, and 'having broken' puts JUG inside it after the E. 'towards' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to strike at the throat's main vein means to attack an opponent's weakest point savagely.

clue.text: Hampshire town's success with soccer, say

parts.note: to make a go of something is to make it a success
soccer is an example of a sport

explanation.surface: A town in southern England boasting of its footballing triumphs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Gosport is a naval town on Portsmouth Harbour in the English county of Hampshire.

clue.text: Discovered near newly-built station: a single piece of masonry

parts.note: discovered means found

indicators.note: something newly built is put together afresh, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: a single means one

explanation.surface: A builder unearths a lone block of stone beside a freshly constructed railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-built' rearranges STATION plus ONE into ATIONSTONE; 'near' just joins FOUND to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial block laid at the start of construction is a particular kind of masonry block.

clue.text: Carpet salesman has to deliver piece for inside

parts.note: rep is short for a sales representative

indicators.note: the piece is placed inside the deliver word

parts.note: to deliver someone from a thing is to rid them of it
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A rug seller has to bring a piece of goods indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is a verb here: to carpet someone is British slang for giving them a dressing-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone, calling them in for a scolding, is to rebuke them formally.

clue.text: Leading trio of Hasidim allowed pork product

indicators.note: the first three letters of the following word are taken

parts.note: allowed means let

explanation.surface: Orthodox Jews being permitted pork would be a surprising ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hasidim keep kosher, which makes a pork product a jarring picture. Haslet is a British meatloaf, from Lincolnshire, made of pork offal.
explanation.definitionFit: Haslet is a seasoned meatloaf of pig offal, eaten cold in slices: a food made from pig meat.

clue.text: Book mentioned German and South American civilisation

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: Jerry is old slang for a German, and the Maya were a civilisation of Central and South America

explanation.surface: A history book that discusses both Germany and an ancient American culture.
explanation.walkthrough: JERRY + MAYA said aloud gives the name of the prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremiah is one of the prophetic books of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Hooligan jailed, inhaling cannabis

indicators.note: the words take in, or contain, the letters needed

explanation.surface: A thug is locked up after being caught smoking dope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inhaling' looks like part of the drug story, but it signals that the answer sits inside 'Hooligan jailed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ganja is a slang name, from Hindi, for marijuana.

clue.text: Small piece of cheese supplied in part of the West End

indicators.note: the small piece is cut from the cheese, so it comes after it

parts.note: Red Leicester is an English cheese
a square is a small piece cut into that shape

explanation.surface: A little cube of cheese is handed out in a theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre and entertainment district.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester Square is a famous plaza in London's West End, home to cinemas and premieres.

clue.text: We're told to continue as author you'll need PC

indicators.note: something we are told is heard, so the phrase is spoken

parts.note: to keep writing is to write on

explanation.surface: Advice to a novelist: keep going, but you'll need a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a personal computer, but here it means politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Right-on is an informal adjective for fashionably liberal or politically correct attitudes.

clue.text: Puzzle's remaining part

definitions.meaning: what is left after something is cut down or worn away

explanation.surface: A jigsaw-like fragment left over at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to baffle (verb), and the leftover base of a tree or limb (noun).

clue.text: Dashing to produce second impression of book

parts.note: an impression is one print run of a book, a printing

explanation.surface: A publisher hurrying to issue a reprint of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second impression' reads as a reprint, but 'second' is just S.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing in the sense of running flat out is a synonym for racing at full speed.

clue.text: Drama initially introduced in O'Neill plays is well-established

indicators.note: the letter is put into the other letters
the name plays about, so its letters are rearranged
only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Eugene O'Neill's plays, with their drama, have become part of the theatrical canon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' rearranges O'NEILL, and 'introduced in' puts D (Drama's first letter) among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-line describes something long-standing and traditional, i.e. long settled.

clue.text: Most humble mate vacated a home

indicators.note: a vacated word is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: taken as written
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A friend moved out of a house, which is about as lowly as it gets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most humble' means lowliest: the superlative of mean in its old sense of low-born.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean once meant of low rank, so its superlative describes the poorest, lowliest station.

clue.text: For example 26, note, and 11

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
the answer to clue 11 means long-standing, as does trad, short for traditional

explanation.surface: A bare cross-reference clue linking two other answers with a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 26-across is a title containing a quartet of feathers, so it is an example of a group of four.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a set of four, and the feathers in 26-across's title number exactly four.

clue.text: Former influential Russian ruler principally like present-day leader

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: as means like
Vladimir Putin is the current Russian leader

explanation.surface: A past Russian strongman compared to the country's current head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' looks like part of the definition, but only its R is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Grigori Rasputin was the mystic who gained great sway over the last Tsar's family.

clue.text: Indicates compass direction's inaccurate

parts.note: a point is one of the directions on a compass, plus S for the 's
out means wrong, as in a calculation that is out

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a compass is giving a wrong reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to draw attention to it, show it to someone.

clue.text: Party-goer climbing on bar, drinking litres

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the letters are read upwards, backwards
the words take in the other letter as a drinker takes in drink

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a lever is a bar used to prise things

explanation.surface: A drunk at a party clambers onto the bar while knocking back litres of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts L into RE + LEVER, making RELLEVER; 'climbing' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveller is someone enjoying a lively celebration, a merrymaker.

clue.text: British gents maybe expired, covered in gore

parts.note: the gents is a men's toilet, an example of a loo
expired means died

explanation.surface: British gentlemen perished in a bloody scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gents' looks like gentlemen, but it is the British word for a men's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodied means stained with blood, which is what gore is.

clue.text: Pompous language in most of old Mumbai thoroughfare

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Bombay is the former name of Mumbai
st is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Grandiloquence heard on a street in old Bombay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops Y from BOMBAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is inflated, high-sounding talk with little substance.

clue.text: Rustic cultivated tree

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over, so the letters are turned about

explanation.surface: A country orchard tree grown by a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus is a genus of tree bearing lemons, oranges and limes.

clue.text: I stray, running into soldiers in mountain ranges

indicators.note: the first letters run into the soldiers, going inside them

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, a British army regiment
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A lost hiker wanders into troops in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierras are long jagged chains of peaks, especially in Spanish-speaking lands.

clue.text: Old European region replacing Liberal with revolutionary? That's awkward

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: Gaul was the ancient region covering modern France
Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A historian awkwardly swaps a political moderate for a radical in an ancient land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing Liberal with revolutionary' swaps the L of GAUL for CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche, French for left, means socially clumsy or tactless.

clue.text: German wine, some briefly knocked back by French female

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters are turned round, as a drink is knocked back
said briefly, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman downing some German wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens SOME to SOM; 'knocked back' turns it to MOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the valley of the river of that name in Germany.

clue.text: Drop building bricks, carrying tons

indicators.note: the bricks carry the letter inside them

parts.note: Lego is the brand of toy building bricks

explanation.surface: Someone drops a heavy load of bricks they were carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop something is to release one's grip on it.

clue.text: Valuable old article stuck to wood, say

indicators.note: the article is attached to the next piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the word is heard

parts.note: teak is a hardwood

explanation.surface: A precious old item glued to a piece of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Valuable old article' reads as one phrase, but 'article' is AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique piece is old and prized for its age, as a collector's piece would be.

clue.text: Like the disciples, a co-pilot's undergoing conversion

indicators.note: the letters are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: An airline co-pilot finds religion, turning into a follower of Jesus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' suits the religious surface but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostolic means relating to the twelve apostles, Jesus's chosen followers.

clue.text: Broadcasting old and new song

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A radio station playing an old song alongside a new one.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme going out live is being transmitted, which is broadcasting.

clue.text: Quartet of chick lit?

parts.note: a novel by A.E.W. Mason whose title names four plumes, as a young bird might shed; chick lit pretends to be the romance genre

explanation.walkthrough: 'chick lit' looks like the genre of light women's fiction, but read literally a quartet of chick's things is the title of a classic adventure novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1902 novel's title names four white plumes, i.e. a quartet of plumage from a bird.
